# Step 2: genomic prediction {#sec-prediction}

::: {.lead}
`02_genomic_prediction.Rmd` compares thirteen evaluation models for NUE, milk urea, Saved Feed and methane, to choose the model on evidence and to measure how well a low-heritability trait like NUE can be predicted.
:::

## The models

| Model | Idea |
|---|---|
| ABLUP | Pedigree only (baseline) |
| GBLUP | Genomic relationships, many small effects |
| ssGBLUP | Single-step: genotyped and non-genotyped animals together, pooled |
| ssGBLUP_MF | Single-step with breed metafounders |
| wssGBLUP | Weighted single-step |
| rrBLUP | Ridge regression on SNP effects |
| BayesA, BayesB | Allow some SNP to have large effects (BGLR) |
| BayesR | SNP effects from a mixture of four normal distributions (zero, small, medium, large); BayesRCO software (Moser et al. 2015) |
| BayesRC_GWAS | BayesR with a separate mixture for a prior SNP set: the 10% of SNPs with the strongest GWAS signal in 1,000 cows that are never used for training or validation (MacLeod et al. 2016) |
| BayesRC_QTL | BayesRC with the SNPs nearest to the largest simulated QTL as the prior set. Not possible with real data; an upper bound for what a perfect biological prior could add |
| JWAS_BayesC | BayesC in JWAS, all breeds pooled (Cheng et al. 2018) |
| JWAS_MT_breeds | Multi-trait BayesC in JWAS with Holstein, Red Dairy and Jersey as three correlated traits, so SNP effects can differ between breeds (Cheng et al. 2018) |

The five models from BayesR on are fitted to the phenotype corrected for herd x generation means, computed from training cows only. They use only genotyped cows, so they compare with GBLUP and the SNP models, not with single-step. They use their own random-number stream, so adding them leaves the results of the other models unchanged (checked).

MTG2 (Lee and van der Werf 2016) and DMU (Madsen and Jensen 2024) are prepared in the code but not yet run: both are distributed by their authors as executables, and they are added once the programs are available.

## How accuracy was measured

- **Validation.** Three-fold cross-validation, plus forward validation in which the youngest cows are predicted from older ones.
- **Accuracy** is the correlation between the estimated and the true breeding value. Only a simulation knows the true value.
- **Within-breed accuracy** is reported, because selection happens within breed. Pooled accuracy is distorted by differences between breed means.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Single-step in a multi-breed population
The genomic (G) and pedigree (A~22~) relationship matrices have different bases. Without adjustment, single-step GBLUP gives breed-level offsets in the breeding values. The pipeline tests an adjusted G and breed metafounders (Vitezica et al. 2011; Legarra et al. 2015).
:::

## What it found

Mean within-breed accuracy of each model (forward and k-fold validation):

{{< include _includes/cv_accuracy.md >}}

A single-step model was the best or within 0.05 of the best in 10 of 10 trait x validation comparisons (the eight shown here plus NUE in the GxE scenario). In the eight comparisons above, a single-step model had the highest within-breed accuracy every time. It is the only family that also uses the records of cows without genotypes. Differences below about 0.05 are within fold-to-fold noise: the standard deviation of k-fold accuracy across folds was up to 0.07 for GBLUP. Weighted single-step gave over-dispersed breeding values.

The five extra models did not improve on GBLUP, the model they compare with:

- **BayesR, BayesRC and both JWAS models** were within 0.05 of GBLUP in all eight comparisons (differences from -0.048 to +0.030).
- **BayesRC_QTL**, with the SNPs next to the largest simulated QTL as the prior set, differed from GBLUP by -0.020 to +0.007. Even a perfect biological prior added nothing here.
- **JWAS_MT_breeds**, with breed-specific SNP effects, differed from pooled JWAS BayesC by -0.03 to +0.02, with no consistent direction.

Full reports: [NUE](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_NUE.html), [milk urea](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_MUN.html), [Saved Feed](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_SF.html), [methane](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_CH4.html).
